Bivariate random-effects model (Hattori's model) estimating the time-dependent SROC curve without publication bias

Source: R/hattori.tsroc.R
hattori.tsroc.Rd

This function estimates the time-dependent SROC curve and SAUC in meta-analysis of prognostic studies, without considering publication bias. At each time point, the time-dependent sensitivity and specificity are reconstructed from the published survival probabilities of the test-positive and test-negative groups, and the bivariate random-effects model of the logit-transformed sensitivity and specificity (with the within-study covariance) is fitted by the maximum likelihood method.

Usage

hattori.tsroc(
  time.points,
  study.os,
  time.os,
  n1.os,
  n0.os,
  s1.os,
  s0.os,
  data.os = NULL,
  study.lnhr,
  lnhr,
  var.lnHR,
  data.lnhr = NULL,
  time.med,
  n1.med,
  n0.med,
  s1.med,
  s0.med,
  data.mt = NULL,
  ci.level = 0.95,
  parallel.ncores = 1L,
  parset = list()
)

Arguments

time.points

A numeric vector of the time points at which the time-dependent SROC curve is estimated. Each value should be included in time.os.

study.os

Specify the column of the study ID (numeric) in data.os.

time.os

Specify the column of the time at which the survival probabilities are reported. The unit of time should be the same as time.points and time.med.

n1.os

Specify the column of the number of subjects in the test-positive group (group 1).

n0.os

Specify the column of the number of subjects in the test-negative group (group 0).

s1.os

Specify the column of the survival probability at time.os in group 1.

s0.os

Specify the column of the survival probability at time.os in group 0.

data.os

A data frame of the survival data, with one row for each study and each time point. Within each study, the rows should be sorted in ascending order of time. If data.os = NULL (default), study.os, time.os, n1.os, n0.os, s1.os, and s0.os are evaluated in the calling environment.

study.lnhr

Specify the column of the study ID (numeric) in data.lnhr, which corresponds to study.os.

lnhr

Specify the column of lnHR (group 1 versus group 0).

var.lnHR

Specify the column of the variance of lnHR.

data.lnhr

A data frame of lnHR, with one row for each study. If data.lnhr = NULL (default), study.lnhr, lnhr, and var.lnHR are evaluated in the calling environment.

time.med

Specify the column of the median follow-up time.

n1.med

Specify the column of the number of subjects in group 1.

n0.med

Specify the column of the number of subjects in group 0.

s1.med

Specify the column of the survival probability at time.med in group 1.

s0.med

Specify the column of the survival probability at time.med in group 0.

data.mt

A data frame of the median follow-up time, with one row for each study reporting it. It is used to estimate the censoring distribution common to all the studies (see details in tsrocsa.lrt). If data.mt = NULL (default), time.med, n1.med, n0.med, s1.med, and s0.med are evaluated in the calling environment.

ci.level

The confidence level of the confidence intervals, within (0, 1). The default is 0.95.

parallel.ncores

The number of cores used for the parallel computation over time.points (PSOCK cluster of the package parallel). The default is 1L (no parallel computation).

parset

A list of the settings for the estimation, which updates the default settings. Bad initial values and bounds may cause non-convergence.

  • inital.values: The initial values of c(mu1, mu2, tau1, tau2, rho). If it is not a vector of length 5 (default), the estimates by mixmeta are used.

  • mu.bound: \(\mu_1\) and \(\mu_2\) are searched within [-mu.bound, mu.bound]. The default is 5.

  • tau.bound: \(\tau_1\) and \(\tau_2\) are searched within [eps, tau.bound]. The default is 5.

  • eps: The lower bound of \(\tau_1\) and \(\tau_2\). The default is 1e-5.

Value

An object of class "sroc": a list with one element for each time point (named "t = xx"). Each element is the same as the output of reitsma.sroc (its data element also contains the within-study covariance v12), or an object of class "try-error" if the estimation failed at that time point. The attributes "call", "ci.level", and "n.study" (the number of studies at each time point) are used by the methods. The results can be shown by print.sroc, summary.sroc, and plot.sroc.

Details

The time-dependent sensitivity and specificity, and their within-study variances and covariance are calculated in the same way as tsrocsa.lrt. study.lnhr, lnhr, and var.lnHR are required as input, but lnHR is not used in the estimation of this function.

References

Hattori, S., & Zhou, X.-H. (2016). Time-dependent summary receiver operating characteristics for meta-analysis of prognostic studies. Statistics in Medicine, 35(26), 4746–4763. doi:10.1002/sim.7029

See also

print.sroc, summary.sroc, plot.sroc, reitsma.sroc, tsrocsa.lrt

Examples

## load data
data(Ki67)
head(Ki67$OS)
#>       author study  t n1 n0   s1    s0
#> 1 bevilacqua     1  6 94 13 1.00 0.990
#> 2 bevilacqua     1 12 94 13 1.00 0.970
#> 3 bevilacqua     1 18 94 13 1.00 0.970
#> 4 bevilacqua     1 24 94 13 0.97 0.965
#> 5 bevilacqua     1 30 94 13 0.92 0.965
#> 6 bevilacqua     1 36 94 13 0.92 0.960
head(Ki67$HR)
#>         author study    HR ci.low  ci.up
#> 1   bevilacqua     1  2.75   1.02   7.39
#> 2         caly     4  1.95   0.92   4.14
#> 3 domagala_no-     5  3.04   1.03   8.99
#> 4 domagala_no+     6  1.38   0.66   2.86
#> 5       erdern     7 17.23   2.42 122.36
#> 6       fresno     8  1.81   0.71   4.59
head(Ki67$MT)
#>       author study  n1  n0 mct_mo s1_mct s0_mct
#> 1 bevilacqua     1  94  13   74.0   0.79   0.84
#> 2     erdern     7  13  34   72.5   0.60   0.97
#> 3     fresno     8  84  62   75.0   0.75   0.90
#> 4    goodson    11  56  56   61.2   0.75   0.90
#> 5     jansen    15 153 168  128.0   0.43   0.60
#> 6     jensen    16  54  64  104.0   0.68   0.90

## Define datasets of the HR
Ki67_OS <- Ki67$OS
Ki67_HR <- Ki67$HR
Ki67_MT <- Ki67$MT

## lnHR and its variance from HR and its 95 percent CI
Ki67_HR$lnHR   <- log(Ki67_HR$HR)
Ki67_HR$lnHR.var <- ((log(Ki67_HR$ci.up) - log(Ki67_HR$ci.low)) / (2 * qnorm(0.975)))^2

fit <- hattori.tsroc(
  time.points = c(24, 36, 60),
  study.os = study,
  time.os = t, n1.os = n1, n0.os = n0,
  s1.os = s1, s0.os = s0,
  data.os = Ki67_OS,
  study.lnhr = study, lnhr = lnHR, var.lnHR = lnHR.var,
  data.lnhr = Ki67_HR,
  time.med = mct_mo, n1.med = n1, n0.med = n0,
  s1.med = s1_mct, s0.med = s0_mct,
  data.mt = Ki67_MT
)

## main results: one row for each time point
fit
#> Time-dependent SROC curve: bivariate random-effects model at each time point
#> (Hattori and Zhou, 2016); publication bias is not considered
#> 
#>         K Conv  SAUC         95% CI  Sens         95% CI  Spec         95% CI
#> t = 24 23  yes 0.713 [0.628, 0.785] 0.743 [0.647, 0.821] 0.562 [0.506, 0.617]
#> t = 36 23  yes 0.651 [0.610, 0.690] 0.662 [0.577, 0.738] 0.570 [0.515, 0.624]
#> t = 60 21  yes 0.647 [0.610, 0.682] 0.630 [0.567, 0.688] 0.587 [0.522, 0.649]
#> 
#> Estimates (tau1, tau2: between-study SDs; rho: correlation):
#>          mu1   mu2  tau1  tau2    rho
#> t = 24 1.063 0.249 0.911 0.520 -0.515
#> t = 36 0.673 0.284 0.656 0.512 -0.877
#> t = 60 0.532 0.353 0.430 0.577 -0.928

## estimates with SEs and confidence intervals at each time point
print(fit)
#> Time-dependent SROC curve: bivariate random-effects model at each time point
#> (Hattori and Zhou, 2016); publication bias is not considered
#> 
#>         K Conv  SAUC         95% CI  Sens         95% CI  Spec         95% CI
#> t = 24 23  yes 0.713 [0.628, 0.785] 0.743 [0.647, 0.821] 0.562 [0.506, 0.617]
#> t = 36 23  yes 0.651 [0.610, 0.690] 0.662 [0.577, 0.738] 0.570 [0.515, 0.624]
#> t = 60 21  yes 0.647 [0.610, 0.682] 0.630 [0.567, 0.688] 0.587 [0.522, 0.649]
#> 
#> Estimates (tau1, tau2: between-study SDs; rho: correlation):
#>          mu1   mu2  tau1  tau2    rho
#> t = 24 1.063 0.249 0.911 0.520 -0.515
#> t = 36 0.673 0.284 0.656 0.512 -0.877
#> t = 60 0.532 0.353 0.430 0.577 -0.928
summary(fit)

## plots
plot(fit, ask = FALSE)                       # all time points, one per page, no prompt



plot(fit, time = 36, add.study = TRUE)       # one time point with the studies

plot(fit, overlay = TRUE)                    # all time points in one panel


# \donttest{
## interactive: press <Return> to move to the next time point
if (interactive()) plot(fit, add.study = TRUE, study.size = "precision")
